page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.large is an entry-level shared-core virtual server instance within the ecs.e4 instance family. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz on x86_64 architecture, this instance features 1 physical core presenting 2 shared vCPUs via hyperthreading. It comes equipped with 16.0 GB of memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance includes no dedicated local storage, lacks bundled GPU accelerators, and provides no baseline public network bandwidth.

Under synthetic CPU benchmarks, the shared vCPU design yields constrained performance, placing in the bottom 10 percent for stress-ng single-core (945.88) and multi-core (1857.99) tests, as well as PassMark CPU scores (2538.35). Memory performance shows uncached read speeds of 14.95 GB/sec and write speeds of 11.46 GB/sec. Despite including hardware instruction flags such as AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, operational execution rates remain reduced due to shared hardware resource allocation.

The primary operational advantage of the ecs.e4.large lies in its high RAM capacity relative to its vCPU count, delivering qualitative cost efficiency for memory-leaning workloads that require minimal compute. However, shared core topology introduces resource contention risks during sustained processor utilization spikes. Application benchmark performance reflects this profile, with static web serving throughput measuring 2.31 GB/sec. This instance is best suited for non-critical development, background caching nodes, light database staging, and low-traffic web services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.large is a shared-core virtual machine instance configured with 2 shared vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM on x86_64 architecture. Built around an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor at 2.5 GHz, it features 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, offering an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory allocation. The instance includes no local disk storage, bundled GPUs, or baseline public networking bandwidth. Benchmark results place its processor and memory throughput in the lower 10th percentile, with stress-ng single-core scoring 945.88 and PassMark CPU at 2538.35. While hardware-accelerated instructions like AVX, AES, and FMA are supported, performance is limited by shared resource contention. The ecs.e4.large offers cost-effective memory density for low-intensity applications, making it suitable for staging environments, lightweight memory caching, and low-traffic web services where sustained compute performance is not required.
